Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning what to do at a crash, the reporting threshold, the safety responsibility law and its filings, mandatory insurance coverages, when you can sue for injury, and the insurance law penalties in plain English.

Prerequisites: the financial responsibility condition for licensing from the first section and the insurance card requirement from the inspection and registration sections.

Scope note: the crash reporting threshold, the ordered duties at a crash scene, information exchange and unattended-vehicle notices, the safety responsibility law with its SR twenty-one and SR twenty-two filings and three-year proof period, mandatory insurance coverages, the conditions for suing over bodily injury, and the insurance law penalties. Alcohol and other drugs follow in the next section.

Recall emphasis: dollar thresholds, coverage amounts, form numbers and the three-year period are practiced as recall items; no scenario or recognition surface is needed for this section.
